transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood SE), Sara Johnson (Acme Head of ML), Tom Wu (Acme Data Eng), Maria Lopez (Acme CTO)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for making time, quick intros, i'm Jordan from Redwood AE side, Carlos is our SE who will lead the benchmarks.
[00:10] Sara: thanks, yes Sara here, i'll be point on the ML side, Tom's our infra lead and Maria is joining to hear the risk/compliance side.
[00:20] Carlos: hi all, quick agenda — scoping success criteria, go over sample workloads, pick an open-model shortlist and agree benchmarks + timeline.
[00:35] Maria: great, our top priorities are data privacy, predictable latency for user-facing features, and cost. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:45] Jordan: understood. can you sketch the POC success criteria? what would make this a win for Acme?
[01:05] Sara: win is threefold: 1) output quality on our analytics summarization and entity extraction matches or exceeds our current internal baseline (we'll provide eval prompts), 2) 95th percentile latency under 800ms for gen with 512 token context for typical user flows, 3) cost per 1k tokens under a threshold — we need numbers but ballpark.
[01:30] Tom: also throughput — we often batch offline jobs, so throughput for embeddings and batch generation matters too.
[01:40] Carlos: good list. for latency target, are we talking hosted API or dedicated? there are differences in SLO.
[01:50] Maria: initially hosted is acceptable but we want the option to move to dedicated if cost/spike behavior causes issues. also data residency — some datasets can't leave region.
[02:05] Jordan: note on residency — Redwood Private or VPC options available; we'll include details in the security packet.
[02:20] Sara: about workloads — Tom, can you give a quick sense of token distribution and sequence lengths?
[02:30] Tom: sure, for the interactive UI median seq is ~120 tokens, 95th ~480, some long reports are 2–3k tokens but offline. Weekly batch embedding jobs have 10M rows but we will sample to POC ~50k.
[02:50] Carlos: that's helpful. so benchmarks should cover three workloads: a) interactive summarization (120–512 context), b) long-document offload (1–3k context, probably chunked), c) batch embeddings (~50k).
[03:10] Sara: exactly. and we need multilingual quality — EN plus Spanish and Japanese for key customers.
[03:20] Jordan: got it. let's talk models. open-model shortlist we propose (based on your needs): OpenLLaMA-3-13B, Redmond-7B-quantized (example internal variant), Mistral-like 7B, and a smaller 3B model for latency baseline. any dislikes or must-haves?
[03:45] Sara: quality is more important for summarization, but latency/cost matter. Spanish/Japanese are critical — do these models support multilingual out of the box?
[03:55] Carlos: tradeoffs — larger models (13B) will generally give better few-shot summarization and multilingual performance but at higher latency/cost. quantized 7B variants can be surprisingly strong on some tasks and much cheaper. we should run evals side-by-side.
[04:15] Tom: can you quantify cost difference? ballpark numbers help us decide dedicated vs hosted.
[04:25] Carlos: we'll include estimated token-level unit costs in the spreadsheet; example: 13B on dedicated optimized runtime might be ~X tokens/sec cost Y, 7B q4 could be ~1/3 the cost with similar latency improvements. exact numbers depend on batching and KV caching; we'll run a sample profiling.
[04:45] Maria: and for security/compliance, what's captured in logs? we need audit logs and ability to disable retention.
[04:55] Jordan: Redwood supports audit logs, configurable retention, and customer-managed KMS for Private. i'll send the SOC2 summary and config options.
[05:10] Sara: on benchmarks, we want both automated quality metrics (ROUGE, BLEU, F1 for entity extraction) and manual spot checks, including multilingual prompt sets.
[05:25] Carlos: yes we'll produce both. we'll use your eval prompts plus our standard scoring harness. also propose we run latency/cost matrix across payload sizes and batching configs.
[05:40] Tom: for batch embedding jobs, do you recommend doing them on Dedicated? we have throughput constraints and cost is a concern.
[05:50] Carlos: embeddings scale well on dedicated; if volume is high Dedicated committed capacity with autoscale is cost-effective, but for POC we can run a limited dedicated pool.
[06:05] Sara: timeline — what is realistic for a POC? we want results within 2–3 weeks if possible.
[06:15] Jordan: realistic plan: week 0 (this week) exchange sample data + prompts; week 1 Carlos sets up runs and shares baseline results; week 2 run extended benchmarks and do manual QA; week 3 review and decision. so 2–3 weeks.
[06:35] Maria: need to review security docs in parallel; please send now.
[06:40] Jordan: will do.
[06:45] Sara: question on multilingual — do you recommend single multilingual model or language-specific models?
[06:55] Carlos: single multilingual 13B may be simplest; for tight latency/cost, using 7B quantized with language-specific fine-tunes could be better. For POC we should test both approaches on your Spanish/Japanese samples.
[07:12] Tom: any constraints about tokenization differences across models? we have some domain tokens and prefer minimal OOV in Spanish domain terms.
[07:25] Carlos: we'll check tokenizer overlap and report unknown token rates; can do quick tokenization pass on your sample corpus.
[07:40] Sara: another question: how will you measure hallucination/regression? We need quality safeguards.
[07:50] Carlos: we'll include hallucination checks using our truth set and targeted prompts; also suggest human-in-the-loop validation for high-risk outputs.
[08:05] Jordan: what about rollout strategy after POC? Acme had mentioned wanting a canary approach.
[08:12] Maria: yes canary then ramp if stable.
[08:20] Jordan: Redwood supports canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models on overloads. will include docs.
[08:30] Sara: ok, to be concrete on models for POC: we propose testing OpenLLaMA-3-13B, Mistral-like-7B, and a quantized 7B variant, plus a 3B baseline for cost/latency. Does that sound right?
[08:45] Carlos: yes, plus we should include a tiny 2–3 model to simulate mobile/offline baseline.
[08:52] Tom: for embeddings, which model do you recommend? we need semantic retrieval across multilingual docs.
[08:58] Carlos: recommend a small dense multilingual embedding model for cost (e.g., open m-embedding-2-small) but we'll confirm candidate. We'll run intralingual and crosslingual tests.
[09:12] Sara: good. on measurement — please provide the benchmark spreadsheet with columns: model, config (quant, batch), p95 latency, median latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, rouge/f1 scores per task, hallucination rate.
[09:30] Carlos: will do; i'll also include per-language breakdowns.
[09:38] Jordan: any blockers to proceed?
[09:45] Tom: just that we need to sanitize PII before sending samples; we'll do that and aim to share by 3/19.
[09:55] Sara: can Redwood run the initial POC on hosted infra first and then repeat on a small dedicated pool for apples-to-apples?
[10:05] Carlos: yes we can run hosted then spin up a small dedicated pool for the same model config — that will highlight differences in latency/cost.
[10:18] Maria: please include KMS options and whether logs can be routed to our SIEM.
[10:25] Jordan: yes, will include SIEM integration notes.
[10:30] Sara: great. any final notes?
[10:35] Jordan: recap of next steps — we'll send security docs, benchmark template, and proposed model list; Acme will send sample datasets and seq histograms; then we'll schedule the benchmark run.
[10:50] Maria: sounds good. thank you.
[10:55] Jordan: thanks all.

Notes: transcription has minor mislabels and filler words. Shared artifacts: "POC_requirements.xlsx" (link in CRM), "benchmark_template.csv" (Carlos to share), SOC2 summary link (Jordan).
